title: Capture byte budgets
responsibility: Streams capture bytes into a digest, reports per-file limit failures, and accounts for bytes admitted to one verification record.

inputs.name: digestFile.path
inputs.description: Path opened read-only with O_NOFOLLOW when available and checked to be a regular file. Open, stat, read, or close failures are thrown.

inputs.name: digestFile.maxBytes
inputs.description: Optional maximum number of bytes the stream may read. Defaults to undefined, meaning no byte ceiling; reading a chunk that takes the total above this value throws before that chunk is hashed or retained.

inputs.name: digestFile.retain
inputs.description: Whether to copy read chunks into the returned contents buffer, which retains the entire file in memory. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: oversizeCapture.file
inputs.description: Capture path inserted into the per-file refusal message when maxCaptureBytes is exceeded.

inputs.name: oversizeCapture.bytes
inputs.description: Observed capture byte count compared with limits.maxCaptureBytes. A count at or below the cap is not refused.

inputs.name: oversizeCapture.limits
inputs.description: Optional byte caps; this function checks maxCaptureBytes and returns no refusal when that cap is absent. maxRecordBytes is not checked here.

inputs.name: RecordBudget.constructor.max
inputs.description: Optional maximum total bytes for retained captures in this record. Defaults to undefined, meaning no record byte ceiling.

inputs.name: RecordBudget.refusal.path
inputs.description: Record-relative capture path inserted into the refusal message if adding the bytes would exceed the record cap.

inputs.name: RecordBudget.refusal.bytes
inputs.description: Capture byte count proposed for addition to the bytes already retained. The method compares their sum with the configured maximum.

inputs.name: RecordBudget.retain.bytes
inputs.description: Byte count to add to the record's used total after the caller admits a capture. The method increments the total without checking the cap.

outputs.name: digestFile
outputs.description: Result containing the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest and number of bytes read; contents is present as a Buffer only when retain is true.

outputs.name: oversizeCapture
outputs.description: Per-file refusal message when bytes exceed maxCaptureBytes, or undefined when no cap is set or the bytes fit.
examples: left capture checks/unit.log of 2097152 bytes, over maxCaptureBytes 1048576 in harness.verify.json; it was not recorded

outputs.name: RecordBudget.remaining
outputs.description: Configured maximum minus bytes already retained, or undefined when the budget has no maximum. It can be negative if the retained total exceeds the maximum.

outputs.name: RecordBudget.refusal
outputs.description: Refusal message when adding the proposed bytes would take the record above its maximum, or undefined when there is no maximum or the sum fits.
examples: left capture checks/typecheck.log of 4096 bytes, which takes the record to 12288 bytes, over maxRecordBytes 8192 in harness.verify.json; it was not recorded

outputs.name: RecordBudget.retain
outputs.description: Void result; the method adds the supplied byte count to the record's used total.

errors.name: Capture read failure
errors.description: digestFile throws file-system errors from opening, checking, reading, or closing the path. It throws Error with message "Capture must be a regular file." when the opened descriptor is not a regular file; O_NOFOLLOW prevents following a final-component symlink when the platform provides that flag.

errors.name: Capture byte limit exceeded
errors.description: digestFile throws Error with message "Capture exceeded maxCaptureBytes or remaining maxRecordBytes while reading." when the bytes read so far exceed maxBytes; the chunk that crosses the ceiling is not hashed or retained.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: digestFile throws Error when the opened descriptor is not a regular file or when bytes read exceed maxBytes. File-system errors from opening, statting, reading, and closing also propagate.
